text.en: Find the notes of line 1: each one waits until you're on it.

text.en: The earliest known printing of its tune, in an early form, is in a Haggadah in Hebrew, Latin and German that J. S. Rittangel, a professor at Königsberg, published in 1644.

source.en: The Jewish Encyclopedia, vol. 1 (1901), "Addir Hu", by Francis L. Cohen, and A. Z. Idelsohn, Jewish Music in its Historical Development (1929), p. 174

text.en: A Judeo-German version, "Allmächtiger Gott, nun bau dein' Tempel schiere" (Almighty God, now build Your Temple soon), was once widely sung, and Gottfried Selig printed it with the tune at Leipzig in 1769.

source.en: A. Z. Idelsohn, Jewish Music in its Historical Development (1929), pp. 174 and 504, and The Jewish Encyclopedia, vol. 1 (1901), "Addir Hu"
